status_reason: The contaminant and the quality variable are undefined, so no method or exact configuration can be approved now; the choice depends on laboratory data not yet collected.
answer: No exact sensor configuration can be approved immediately, because the contaminant and quality variable are not yet named and the method choice depends on them. Test NIR first in a laboratory screen of on-spec and off-spec samples, with Raman as the comparison, and specify probe, install point and fiber only after one method separates the off-spec samples. A NIR + Raman combination is a hypothesis to test later against the best single method.

inline.headline: Test NIR in a laboratory screen of on-spec and off-spec samples before any in-line installation
inline.probe: NIR transmission or transflection probe for liquids, path 1-10 mm (candidate only, not final)
inline.install: not yet; after the laboratory screen, at a process point the client defines (location not stated)
inline.fiber: silica Vis-NIR fiber (350-2400 nm); the NIR range runs to 2500 nm, so check the fiber for the band actually needed
inline.not_final_because: the contaminant and quality variable are unknown, so the method is not yet proven; NIR bands overlap and need a chemometric model built and validated on reference data; the silica fiber range ends at 2400 nm while NIR is listed up to 2500 nm

problems.text: An exact configuration is requested before the analytical problem is known: the contaminant and quality variable are not named, and the method selection depends on them.
It is assumed one method will be enough; for samples of incompletely known composition it is not possible to predict which method will work, so several methods must be tested.
Fluorescence cannot be assumed to detect the problem, because most chemicals do not fluoresce and it relies on secondary emission of certain substances.
Occasional off-spec events are not yet linked to any measured variable; without on-spec and off-spec samples with reference results, no model can be built or validated.

methods.why: the most common online fiber-probe method, with transmission and transflection probes suited to liquids, but its broad overlapping bands need chemometrics.
carries information complementary to MIR and has high selectivity, but needs special probes and can be masked by fluorescence.
gives well-defined absorption peaks and suits liquids through ATR probes with high-transmission MIR fibers, but MIR is limited to very thin layers.
highly sensitive, but only useful if the contaminant or quality variable emits fluorescence.

questions.q: What is the suspected contaminant, or which quality variable goes off specification?
questions.why: the analytical problem decides the method, and no method can be chosen without it.

questions.q: What is the specification limit and the process concentration range of the quality variable?
questions.why: the required sensitivity depends on how close the limit is to normal operation; NIR may lack sensitivity at low levels.

questions.q: Is the liquid transparent, turbid, or does it contain solids or bubbles?
questions.why: transparent liquids suit transmission or transflection probes, while opaque or turbid media need a different probe type.

questions.q: Where in the process would a probe go, and what are the temperature, pressure and flow there?
questions.why: the install point and fiber construction depend on these conditions.

questions.q: Do you have historical on-spec and off-spec samples with independent laboratory results?
questions.why: these are needed to test whether a method sees the difference and to build a validated model.

experiment.objective: Find out which method sees the difference between on-spec and off-spec samples before any in-line configuration is chosen.
steps: Collect on-spec and off-spec samples and have the suspected contaminant or quality variable measured by an independent laboratory method.
Measure the same samples in the laboratory with NIR, Raman, MIR ATR and, if the chemistry allows, fluorescence.
Check with multivariate analysis whether each method separates on-spec from off-spec samples, and record the key spectral features.
Build chemometric models on the best method and validate them with segmented cross-validation and randomisation tests.
Test a combination only if no single method is sufficient, and compare it against the best single method on the same validation data.
experiment.go_no_go: criteria come from the client; no threshold is set in this assessment

pathway.key_features: to be identified from laboratory spectra; none measured yet
pathway.path_reason: key spectral features are not selected yet, and the guided pathway begins with a multi-method laboratory test.

multispectral.why: NIR responds to polar groups and hydrogen bonds while Raman responds to the molecular backbone and non-polar groups, so their information is complementary.
multispectral.test: build the NIR-only and Raman-only models and the fused NIR + Raman model on the same validation data; the combination is accepted only if it beats the best single method, as the feed-frame study reported for API potency in that study.

assumptions: The liquid is assumed transparent enough for a transmission or transflection test until its appearance is checked.
Reference values for chemometric models will come from an independent laboratory analysis, not from the instrument's own calibration.
The process point for any future probe is assumed to be reachable by a flush-mounted or inline probe; the location was not stated.
